newsitem.title: MEXICO: J.P. Morgan strengthens Mexico peso forecast.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan strengthens Mexico peso forecast.

text.p: J.P. Morgan forecast that Mexico's peso will end the year at 8.6 per U.S. dollar, revising its previous forecast of 9.1 pesos per dollar, the firm said in a report released on Monday.
The revision reflected expectations of stronger economic growth and a move by the central bank to boost reserves and to sell dollars if the need arises, the report said.
"The peso will react most to the economy's veritable boom last quarter and likely continued strength all through 1997," economist Alfredo Thorne wrote.
Mexico's gross domestic product grew at a 7.6 percent rate in the fourth quarter of 1996, the government said last week.
The peso should react to a lapse into deficit in the external trade balance, caused by rising consumption, he said, but added that currencies take time to reach new equilibria.
He added that Banco de Mexico's decision to raise the size of its monthly reserve purchases and to sell dollars if the peos depreciates two percent or more in a day could damp peso volatility.
The mechanisms could delay any correction of the peso.
"J.P. Morgan believes that the relevant signals will not become convincing until October. In turn, full exchange rate correction may extend beyond year-end," Thorne wrote.

He said the firm saw the peso sliding slightly to the weak side of 8.0 per dollar by the end of July, and then to about 8.6 per dollar between late September and late December because of a variety of negative factors, including a decline in real interest rates later in the year
